answer: One way an agent economy resists Sybil attacks is stake-slash bonds. Every identity must lock a deposit before it can transact, and misbehavior burns it - the slash cuts like pigment through velvet, staining the attacker's ledger permanently. Each identity also keeps a heartbeat: a regular pulse of signed activity proving a live operator rather than a scripted swarm. Forging N identities then costs N bonds plus N heartbeats to maintain, so the attacker's expense scales linearly with every fake while the network's cost to verify a bond stays constant.
